projects.title: Volunteer shift scheduling
projects.description: Bayview Community Pantry runs its weekly food distribution with about 60 volunteers, coordinated through a shared spreadsheet and group texts. Shifts are often double-booked or left empty, and the coordinator spends hours each week chasing replacements. The team will map how volunteers currently sign up and swap shifts, then design a simpler way to see open slots and get reminders. Likely deliverables are a working sign-up prototype, a one-page guide for the coordinator, and a short report on what volunteers said they need.

projects.title: Tenant rights info hub
projects.description: Mission Housing Collective answers the same tenant questions every week: rent increases, repairs, deposits and eviction notices. The information exists, but it is spread across legal PDFs that most tenants find hard to read. The team will interview tenants and staff to find the most common questions and rewrite the answers in plain language, in English and Spanish. Deliverables could include a mobile-friendly info site, printable one-page handouts, and a plan for keeping the content up to date.

projects.title: Youth coding club curriculum
projects.description: Eastside Learning Center wants to start an after-school coding club for 12 to 15 year olds but has no curriculum and volunteer teachers with mixed experience. The team will research beginner-friendly approaches, test sample lessons with a small group of students, and see what keeps them coming back. The aim is an eight-week curriculum that a non-expert volunteer can run. Deliverables are lesson plans with slides, a starter project for each week, and a short facilitator guide.

projects.title: Library e-resource onboarding
projects.description: Northgate Public Library pays for e-books, language courses and research databases, but most members don't know they exist or give up at the login step. The team will watch members try to get started, find where they get stuck, and work with librarians on what to promote first. Deliverables could include a redesigned getting-started page, short how-to videos or guides, and a sign-up flow tested with real members.

projects.title: Urban garden plot booking
projects.description: Green Blocks Initiative manages 40 community garden plots across three sites, with bookings tracked on paper and a long waitlist kept by email. Gardeners don't know when plots free up, and staff can't easily see who is using what. The team will design a fair, simple way to join the waitlist, claim a plot and renew each season. Deliverables are a booking prototype, a proposal for waitlist rules, and a handover guide for staff.

projects.title: Senior tech help desk
projects.description: Golden Years Network gets constant requests from older members for help with phones, video calls, scams and online forms. Volunteers help when they can, but there is no way to track requests or share answers to common problems. The team will look at what members ask for most and how help is given today, then design a drop-in and phone help-desk process. Deliverables could include a request-tracking setup, a library of large-print how-to guides, and training notes for volunteers.

projects.title: Bike repair co-op inventory
projects.description: Spokes Together repairs donated bikes and sells parts at low cost, but its inventory lives in volunteers' heads and a whiteboard. Parts are reordered twice or run out mid-repair, and nobody knows what stock is worth. The team will spend time in the shop to understand how parts move, then build a simple way to log what comes in and goes out. Deliverables are an inventory tool suited to a busy workshop, a labeling system for shelves, and a monthly stock report template.

projects.title: Refugee job board
projects.description: New Roots Alliance helps newly arrived refugees find work, but job leads arrive by phone, email and word of mouth and are hard to match to the right person. Many clients are still learning English and use a phone as their only device. The team will interview caseworkers, clients and local employers to understand what a good match looks like. Deliverables could include a mobile-first job board prototype, a simple process for employers to post roles, and translated guides for clients.

projects.title: Clinic wait-time tracker
projects.description: Harborview Free Clinic sees walk-in patients on a first-come basis, and people often wait hours without knowing how long it will be. Some leave before being seen, and front-desk staff field constant questions. The team will observe intake on clinic days and talk to patients and staff about what would help. Deliverables are a prototype that shows estimated wait times by text or on a screen, a revised intake process, and data on how wait times change through the day.

projects.title: Neighborhood safety map
projects.description: Westside Residents Association hears about broken streetlights, unsafe crossings and dumping, but reports go to different city departments and residents rarely hear back. The association wants a clear picture of where the problems are so it can push for fixes. The team will gather existing reports, run a short resident survey, and design a way to collect and map new ones. Deliverables could include an interactive map, a reporting form, and a summary of the top issues for the association to bring to the city.

projects.title: Food waste pickup routing
projects.description: Second Plate collects surplus food from restaurants and grocery stores and delivers it to shelters, using volunteer drivers and routes planned by hand each morning. Pickups are missed when plans change, and drivers often cross the city twice. The team will study a few weeks of pickup data and ride along with drivers to understand the constraints. Deliverables are a routing approach that reduces driving time, a simple daily schedule view for drivers, and a short report on the savings.

projects.title: Arts grant application helper
projects.description: City Arts Fund offers small grants to local artists, but many first-time applicants give up or submit incomplete applications. Staff spend a lot of time answering the same questions about eligibility and budgets. The team will review past applications, interview artists who applied and some who didn't, and find where the process loses people. Deliverables could include a step-by-step application guide, an eligibility checker, and recommendations to simplify the form itself.

projects.title: Transit access guide
projects.description: Bay Rides Coalition advocates for riders with disabilities, who often can't tell in advance whether a station has a working elevator or step-free access. Information is scattered across agency websites and is often out of date. The team will audit a set of key stations and interview riders about how they plan trips today. Deliverables are an accessible station guide, a way for riders to report broken elevators, and a summary of findings the coalition can share with transit agencies.

projects.title: Shelter bed availability board
projects.description: Oakland Open Door works with several local shelters, and outreach workers spend hours calling around each evening to find an open bed for someone. By the time a bed is found it is sometimes already gone. The team will talk to shelter staff and outreach workers to understand how beds are held and released. Deliverables could include a shared availability board shelters can update in seconds, a phone-friendly view for outreach workers, and an agreement on how often counts are refreshed.

projects.title: After-school tutor matching
projects.description: Richmond Reads pairs volunteer tutors with elementary students who are behind in reading, but matching is done by one staff member using a spreadsheet. Pairs are often poorly matched on schedule or language, and many end in the first month. The team will look at past matches and interview tutors, families and teachers. Deliverables are a matching process with clear criteria, a sign-up form for tutors and families, and a check-in routine to catch struggling pairs early.

projects.title: Small business grant finder
projects.description: Fruitvale Merchants Group supports small, mostly family-run businesses that miss out on grants because they don't hear about them or find the paperwork overwhelming. Opportunities are posted in many places with different rules. The team will gather current local, state and federal programs and interview business owners about what stops them applying. Deliverables could include a searchable grant finder, plain-language summaries of the top programs, and a calendar of upcoming deadlines.

projects.title: Community fridge tracker
projects.description: Sunset Mutual Aid runs four community fridges that neighbors stock and use freely. Volunteers have no easy way to know which fridges are empty, full or need cleaning, so some sit bare while others overflow. The team will visit the fridges, talk to volunteers and users, and design a light-touch way to report status. Deliverables are a status-reporting prototype such as a QR code at each fridge, a volunteer rota, and a short guide for setting up new fridges.

projects.title: Wetlands volunteer log
projects.description: Baylands Stewards runs weekend restoration days where volunteers remove invasive plants and plant natives, but hours and work done are recorded on paper sign-in sheets. The organization needs better records to report to funders and track restoration over time. The team will go to a workday and design a quick way to log volunteers, hours and areas worked. Deliverables could include a mobile logging tool that works with weak signal, a dashboard of hours and acres, and a funder report template.

projects.title: Immigrant legal clinic intake
projects.description: San Jose Legal Access holds free immigration clinics where volunteers collect long intake forms by hand before clients can see a lawyer. The process takes so long that some clients leave before their consultation. The team will observe a clinic and work with staff on which questions are really needed up front. Deliverables are a shorter, multilingual intake form, a process that lets clients start before arriving, and guidance for handling sensitive information safely.

projects.title: Veteran benefits navigator
projects.description: Marin Veterans Hub helps veterans and their families claim benefits for healthcare, housing and education, but the eligibility rules are complex and change often. Many veterans don't know what they qualify for until a caseworker sits down with them. The team will interview veterans and caseworkers and map the most common benefit journeys. Deliverables could include a guided questionnaire that suggests likely benefits, plain-language guides for the top programs, and a checklist of documents to bring.

events.title: CCP Kick-Off
events.description:
Introduction to CCP, your team and your project. Attendance at your session is required and no make-up work is available.

M30s in San Francisco: in person, 10:00 am to 1:00 pm PT.

Groups 22 and 23 (predominantly M30s in Buenos Aires): 7:00 to 9:00 am UTC, see the Google Calendar invitation.

Group 24 (most VSYs): 2:00 to 4:00 pm UTC, see the Google Calendar invitation.

events.title: Workshop 1: Problem framing
events.description:
Most projects struggle not because the solution is wrong but because the problem was never clearly defined. In this workshop, each team turns its partner's broad challenge into a specific problem statement it can actually test.

We'll work through three short exercises: mapping who is affected, separating symptoms from causes, and writing a "How might we" question. By the end, every team should have one problem statement it agrees on.

Bring your partner brief and a laptop. Teams will share their statements at the end for quick feedback.

events.title: Partner meet & greet
events.description:
An informal online call to meet the partner organizations behind this cohort's projects. Each partner will spend a few minutes on who they are, the work they do and why they brought their challenge to the program.

There will be time for questions at the end, so come with anything you'd like to know about your partner's goals, constraints or the people they serve. The call is optional but strongly recommended if you haven't spoken with your partner yet.

The recording will be shared afterwards for anyone who can't join.

events.title: Workshop 2: User research
events.description:
Before building anything, you need to hear from the people your project is for. This session covers how to find interviewees, how to ask open questions without leading people toward the answer you want, and how to take notes your whole team can use.

The second half is practice: teams pair up and run short mock interviews with each other, then swap roles. You'll leave with an interview guide and a plan to talk to at least five people before the next workshop.

events.title: Workshop 3: Prototyping
events.description:
Now that you understand the problem, it's time to make something people can react to. This workshop is about building quick, rough versions of your idea, like paper sketches, clickable mockups or a simple role-play, before investing weeks into a polished solution.

We'll look at examples of good and bad prototypes, then teams will have about an hour in the maker lab to build their first one. Materials are provided, including paper, markers, sticky notes and a few tablets.

The goal is not perfection. If your prototype takes more than an hour to make, it's probably too detailed.

events.title: Social night
events.description:
A relaxed evening with food, music and games, and no work talk required. It's a chance to get to know people from other teams, swap stories about how your projects are going and meet some of the mentors outside of workshops.

Vegetarian and vegan options will be available. Friends and partners are welcome to come along.

events.title: Weekly team check-in
events.description:
A short weekly meeting where each team shares what they did last week, what they plan to do next and anything they're stuck on.

Keep it to two minutes per team. Mentors will stay afterwards for anyone who wants help.

events.title: Workshop 4: Testing with users
events.description:
Time to put your prototype in front of real users and find out what works. We'll cover how to run a short testing session, what to watch for while someone uses your prototype and how to avoid explaining it too much.

Each team will then run at least two live tests with invited guests during the session. At the end, teams will sort what they saw into what to keep, change and drop, and decide on next steps before the midpoint showcase.

Please bring your latest prototype and make sure it's ready to be tested.

events.title: Midpoint showcase
events.description:
The midpoint showcase is where each team presents its progress to partners, mentors and the rest of the cohort. Every team gets five minutes to present followed by three minutes of questions.

Cover the problem you're working on, what you've learned from users so far, what your prototype looks like now and what you plan to do in the second half of the program. Slides are optional; a short demo is encouraged.

Partners will give written feedback to each team after the event. Please send your slides, if any, to the program team by noon on the day.

events.title: Final Project Proposal Presentations
events.description:
A 10-minute presentation plus 5 minutes of Q&A with your Civic Partner and Faculty Grader. The schedule will be released closer to presentation time.

Presentations are on Zoom, so you must be available with a reliable internet connection during your assigned time.
